newsitem.title: USA: Federal safety regulators open wiper probe.
newsitem.headline: Federal safety regulators open wiper probe.

text.p: Federal safety regulators said Monday they were looking into complaints of faulty windshield wipers on about 1 million 1992-93 Chrysler Corp. minivans.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in its monthly defect investigation report that it has received 13 complaints of windshield wipers flying off the windshield while being used in a rainstorm.

NHTSA launched its probe after receiving a request from the Center for Auto Safety, a Washington-based consumer safety group. The center said there have been "several hundred" complaints about windshield wiper arms on certain 1989-97 Chrysler vehicles. But NHTSA said a database search turned up only 13 complaints concerning detached or loose wiper arms.

Safety regulators also said they opened an initial investigation into 60,500 1995 Chrysler Cirrus and Dodge Stratus sedans. NHTSA has received three complaints that the front suspension may collapse because of a lower control arm ball joint failure.

Chrysler spokesman Jason Vines said the company cannot comment on the wiper issue because it has not received formal notification from NHTSA. Regarding the suspension complaints, Vines said the automaker continues to work with NHTSA to resolve the issue.
In other actions, NHTSA said it is investigating 65,500 1995-96 Ford Motor Co. Explorer sport utility vehicles for complaints of electrical fires that have injured one person.
NHTSA said it has received eight complaints of a fire starting from the center console. Some of the reports suggest the auxiliary power port may be involved.
Regulators are also looking at 1986-91 Volvo 200, 700 and 900 Series cars because of six complaints of passenger compartment fires.
Officials from Ford and Volvo could not be reached for comment.

Also Monday, Ford announced three recalls covering 638,100 vehicles. The largest affects 445,300 1991-94 Lincoln Continentals, and 1991-95 Taurus and Sable sedans, the latter with 3.8-liter engines and speed control.
Ford said in freezing temperatures the speed control cable may freeze and not allow the engine to return to idle. The recalls affect vehicles in 23 northern states, as well as 57,300 in Canada.

Ford said it is recalling 1992-97 Ford Crown Victoria police and taxi vehicles because the hood latch striker may either wear or become detached, causing the hood to flip open when the car is moving. Approximately 191,000 vehicles are involved, of which 6,000 are located in Canada.

Ford said it is recalling 1,800 1996-97 Ford Contour small cars equipped with the compressed natural gas bi-fuel option to disable the option. Ford said it is possible a backfire could occur when the engine is started on compressed natural gas, causing damage to plastic components in the air intake and air cleaner system.
